import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')

# Create a figure with multiple subplots for comprehensive visualization
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 12))
fig.suptitle('Dog Registration Analysis in Zurich, Switzerland', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold')

# 1. Top 10 Dog Breeds
ax1 = axes[0, 0]
breed_counts = df['Rasse1Text'].value_counts().head(10)
colors1 = sns.color_palette('viridis', 10)
bars1 = ax1.barh(breed_counts.index[::-1], breed_counts.values[::-1], color=colors1)
ax1.set_xlabel('Number of Dogs', fontsize=10)
ax1.set_ylabel('Breed', fontsize=10)
ax1.set_title('Top 10 Most Popular Dog Breeds', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
for i, v in enumerate(breed_counts.values[::-1]):
    ax1.text(v + 50, i, str(v), va='center', fontsize=9)

# 2. Dogs by District (Kreis)
ax2 = axes[0, 1]
district_counts = df.groupby('KreisLang')['AnzHunde'].sum().sort_values(ascending=True)
colors2 = sns.color_palette('mako', len(district_counts))
bars2 = ax2.barh(district_counts.index, district_counts.values, color=colors2)
ax2.set_xlabel('Number of Dogs', fontsize=10)
ax2.set_ylabel('District', fontsize=10)
ax2.set_title('Dog Distribution by District', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

# 3. Dog Age Distribution
ax3 = axes[1, 0]
# Filter out any extreme values and use numeric age
age_data = df[df['AlterVHundNum'].notna() & (df['AlterVHundNum'] <= 20)]
sns.histplot(data=age_data, x='AlterVHundNum', bins=21, kde=True, ax=ax3, color='steelblue', alpha=0.7)
ax3.set_xlabel('Dog Age (Years)', fontsize=10)
ax3.set_ylabel('Count', fontsize=10)
ax3.set_title('Age Distribution of Registered Dogs', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax3.axvline(age_data['AlterVHundNum'].mean(), color='red', linestyle='--', label=f'Mean: {age_data["AlterVHundNum"].mean():.1f} years')
ax3.legend()

# 4. Dog Gender Distribution by Owner Gender
ax4 = axes[1, 1]
# Create a crosstab of owner gender and dog gender
gender_cross = pd.crosstab(df['SexLang'], df['SexHundLang'])
# Ensure we have the columns we need
if 'männlich' in gender_cross.columns and 'weiblich' in gender_cross.columns:
    gender_cross = gender_cross[['männlich', 'weiblich']]
    gender_cross.plot(kind='bar', ax=ax4, color=['#3498db', '#e74c3c'], alpha=0.8, width=0.7)
    ax4.set_xlabel('Owner Gender', fontsize=10)
    ax4.set_ylabel('Number of Dogs', fontsize=10)
    ax4.set_title('Dog Gender by Owner Gender', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
    ax4.legend(title='Dog Gender', labels=['Male', 'Female'])
    ax4.set_xticklabels(['Male Owner', 'Female Owner'], rotation=0)
else:
    # Fallback: Show dog gender distribution
    dog_gender = df['SexHundLang'].value_counts()
    ax4.pie(dog_gender.values, labels=dog_gender.index, autopct='%1.1f%%', colors=['#3498db', '#e74c3c'])
    ax4.set_title('Dog Gender Distribution', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
